properties.content: Question: egg allergy influenza vaccine Answer: Can people with egg allergies receive the influenza vaccine? Yes, most people with egg allergies can safely receive the influenza vaccine. Explanation:: - Most influenza vaccines are produced using eggs, which contain a small amount of egg protein called ovalbumin. - However, the amount of ovalbumin in the vaccine is very small and usually does not cause a reaction in people with egg allergies. - Studies have shown that the risk of an allergic reaction to the influenza vaccine in people with egg allergies is extremely low. - In fact, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that all people with egg allergies, regardless of the severity of their allergy, receive the influenza vaccine. Special Considerations:: - In rare cases, people with severe egg allergies may experience an allergic reaction after receiving the influenza vaccine. - If you have a severe egg allergy, it is recommended that you receive the vaccine in a healthcare setting where there is access to medical care in case of an allergic reaction. - There are also egg-free influenza vaccines available, which may be an option for people with very severe egg allergies. Conclusion: Most people with egg allergies can safely receive the influenza vaccine. It is important to consult with a healthcare provider to discuss the best vaccination option for your individual needs.
